hints: Use 2=log₄(16) and the power law on 2log₄(3x−1).
Combine the logarithms and equate their positive arguments to obtain 16(2x+1)=(3x−1)².
Expand and collect terms to display the required quadratic in x.
walkthrough:
Express the constant 2 as a base-4 logarithm:
$$2 = \log_4\left(4^2\right) = \log_4(16)$$

Apply the power law of logarithms to $2\log_4(3x - 1)$:
$$2\log_4(3x - 1) = \log_4\left((3x - 1)^2\right)$$

Combine the right-hand side using the quotient rule for logarithms:
$$\log_4\left((3x - 1)^2\right) - \log_4(16) = \log_4\left(\dfrac{(3x - 1)^2}{16}\right)$$
$$\log_4(2x + 1) = \log_4\left(\dfrac{(3x - 1)^2}{16}\right)$$

Remove logarithms by equating the arguments:
$$2x + 1 = \dfrac{(3x - 1)^2}{16}$$

Multiply by 16 and expand both sides:
$$16(2x + 1) = (3x - 1)^2$$
$$32x + 16 = 9x^2 - 6x + 1$$

hints: Solve the quadratic obtained in part (a) exactly.
Check both roots against 2x+1>0 and 3x−1>0 from the original logarithms.
Retain only admissible roots and give the non-exact value to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Calculate decimal values for both roots:
$$x_1 = \dfrac{19 + 4\sqrt{31}}{9} \approx \dfrac{19 + 4(5.567764)}{9} = \dfrac{41.271057}{9} \approx 4.58567 \approx 4.59$$
$$x_2 = \dfrac{19 - 4\sqrt{31}}{9} \approx \dfrac{19 - 22.271057}{9} = \dfrac{-3.271057}{9} \approx -0.36345$$

Check domain constraints for the logarithms in the original equation:
$$\text{Condition 1: } 3x - 1 > 0 \implies x > \dfrac{1}{3} \approx 0.333$$
$$\text{Condition 2: } 2x + 1 > 0 \implies x > -\dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Since } x_2 \approx -0.363 < \dfrac{1}{3}, \text{ the argument } 3x_2 - 1 < 0, \text{ so reject } x_2.$$
$$\text{For } x_1 \approx 4.59 > \dfrac{1}{3}, \text{ all arguments are positive and valid.}$$

State the unique valid solution correct to 3 significant figures:
$$x = \dfrac{19 + 4\sqrt{31}}{9} \approx 4.59$$
